Issued at 102 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

Water vapor imagery indicates a shortwave trough axis near
Florida this morning, with clear upper divergence ahead of the
feature. Fresh onshore flow persists in the boundary layer, with
Florida residing in a tight pressure gradient to the south of a
surface high over the Mid-Atlantic. PWAT (total moisture) values
are around 2 inches, which is well above early November norms. A
well-defined MCV sits south of Orlando; it has enhanced the 
upward motion and deep moisture convergence over Central and South
Florida during the last 12 to 18 hours. The overall setup will 
change little through today.

Later tonight and into Tuesday, the shortwave trough is expected
to weaken as it nearly stalls over Florida. Gradually, the
pressure gradient will start to relax on Tuesday and especially
Wednesday. Still, above-normal moisture is forecast to remain
situated over Florida through the middle of the week.

The global ensembles continue to track a pair of shortwaves in the
subtropical jet over the Central U.S. later this week. The first one
is forecast to reach the Mid-Mississippi Valley on Thursday before
quickly weakening as it runs into a ridge along the East Coast. The
second feature, fast on its heels, passes north of Florida on
Friday. A diffuse cold front may reach the state on Friday as it
moves by. Little cold air advection is expected behind this front,
and moisture levels only drop closer to seasonal averages.

Guidance favors a more significant pattern change beginning
late this weekend into early next week. As ridging shifts to the
Western U.S., ensemble means support a developing trough over the
southern Mississippi Valley by Sunday. Cluster analysis of the
01/12Z guidance shows considerable spread in trough timing and
amplitude. However, more than half of members support a cold front
reaching the state around next Monday. Briefly, deeper moisture
looks to be advected ahead of the front. H85 (5kft) temperatures are
expected to fall below normal behind the boundary by next Tuesday
(Nov 10th).

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Now - Tonight...

Bands of heavy rain and isolated lightning continue to develop
early this morning along the coast from Brevard County northward,
extending into Greater Orlando. As mentioned in the overview,
the setup remains favorable for heavy rain and localized flooding
through at least this morning, but hi-res guidance continues
to disagree on how quickly the flooding threat will end later
today. For this reason, we have opted to continue the Flood Watch
for all of east central Florida through 7 pm.

This disturbance has already proven its ability to drop copious
rainfall amounts, evidenced by the flash flooding that took place
near Okeechobee and West Palm Beach on Sunday. Through tonight,
an additional 1-3" of rain is forecast, with a 5-10% chance of
additional amounts exceeding 5 inches. Exact placement of these
heavy rain bands is difficult, and our available guidance has
continued to struggle with the evolution of this event. Our soil
saturation model shows greater than 80% saturation from Brevard
County southward before exceeding 90-95% along the Treasure
Coast to Okeechobee. These areas remain particularly vulnerable
to flash flooding, as saturated soils have limited capacity to
absorb additional rainfall, increasing the potential for rapid
runoff and localized inundation.

Later this afternoon and into tonight, we expect rain coverage
to drop somewhat, though moisture remains sufficient for locally 
heavy downpours through the night.

Finally, beach conditions remain hazardous. The High Surf Advisory
will continue until early this evening for 5-7 ft breakers,
and numerous life-threatening rip currents are likely. Minor
to moderate coastal flooding remains possible, especially this
afternoon during high tide south of St Lucie Inlet.

Tuesday - Wednesday...

As the disturbance responsible for all of this rain stalls over
us and weakens, ample moisture will remain in place for a few
showers and/or isolated storms. Coverage should range from 40-60%
on Tuesday to 30-50% on Wednesday. Generally speaking, lighter
amounts are forecast, which should limit excessive rainfall and
flooding concerns. Easterly breezes will continue, though speeds
and gusts will begin to relax a bit.

Some additional sunshine will allow high temps to bounce back into
the low to mid 80s.

Thursday and beyond...

Deep-layer moisture continues to lessen later this week and into the
weekend, limiting rain chances to 20% or less each day. Tranquil
conditions will finally allow some drying to take place over all
of Central Florida. High temps should remain warm in the low to
mid 80s, but the slightly less humid air will mean cooler nights
with 60s for most spots.
